answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake bond before trading, verified against a public work history. Like a reef that only grows where real coral settles, reputation accrues slowly from completed, attested jobs, not from self-declared claims. A whisper of suspicion from peers triggers an audit: if the agent's quill-signed record shows fabricated work, the bond is slashed and the identity burned. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of bonds, while honest agents earn their stake back.
